Attaching the kernel & KV tracing summary along with batch composition. Key findings in brief:
- Fallback to slower attention kernel at seq-length >= 512 which increases p95 latency by ~3.8x for affected batches.
- Fallback rate spikes when batch has a mix of short (<=128) and long (>=512) requests; our continuous batching grouped heterogeneous sequences during the 02:30 UTC window.
- A small tokenization mismatch with the latest tokenizer table led to off-by-one decoding for ~0.8% of requests (explains malformed outputs).

We recommend:
A) Immediate rollback to qprofile v2.2 (we can perform a rolling rollback in the next 30 minutes).
B) Short-term remedial: pin tokenizer tables for Zenridge to the previous build and add a soft filter to isolate long-sequence requests into a separate batch queue (reduces kernel fallback mixing).
C) Post-mortem changes: add a preflight batch-sim test to the qprofile rollout pipeline to simulate heterogeneous batching.

Attachments included: profile-diff.csv, kernel-trace-summary.txt, error-samples.txt
